summary.headline: Artemis Q2 FY27 revenue rose 13.2% YoY to INR 311 crore; Gurugram hit record 23.8% EBITDA margin while new Raipur hospital ramps from 10% occupancy.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR 311 crore (up 13.2% YoY) with reported EBITDA of INR 62.89 crore (20.2% margin) and adjusted operational EBITDA of INR 71.5 crore (23.3%). PAT was INR 31 crore, up 3.7% YoY. H1 FY27 revenue was INR 598.4 crore (up 13% YoY) and H1 PAT was INR 62.5 crore (up 22.2%). Artemis Shanti Hospital in Raipur (300 beds) began operations in July 2026 and is loss-making at about INR 9 crore in its first quarter, while management reiterated the South Delhi and Gurugram Tower 4 expansion timelines.

financial_highlights.value: INR 9 crore; revenue INR 5.3 crore vs INR 4.3 crore estimate; operating cost about INR 10 crore incl. fixed

segments.name: Gurugram hospital
segments.commentary: Recorded its highest-ever EBITDA margin at 23.8% in Q2 at 68% occupancy; management targets 75% occupancy with cost points broadly unchanged.

segments.name: Artemis Shanti Hospital, Raipur (300 beds)
segments.commentary: Started operations July 2026 with about 10% occupancy at the time of the call; ARPOB about INR 30,000-32,000 vs competitor benchmark of INR 26,000-27,000. Breakeven guided at 12-15 months.

segments.name: Artemis Cardiac Care
segments.commentary: Positive EBITDA of about INR 70 lakh and PAT of about INR 20 lakh in the quarter; management plans 4-5 more units after the fundraise-funded bigger hospitals.

segments.name: International patients
segments.commentary: Contributed approximately 30% of revenue in the quarter, drawn from more than 150 countries.

guidance_outlook: Raipur occupancy expected to reach 20-25%, possibly 30%, in coming quarters; ARPOB ramp toward management's earlier INR 55,000-58,000 aspiration is noted as possible.
Raipur breakeven guided at 12-15 months, with internal target to beat it; costs expected to be largely in place, with only minor nursing additions.
Gurugram Tower 4 adds 250 beds in one phase by H2 FY28, taking beds from about 700 to 900-plus.
South Delhi Lajpat Nagar project (650-plus beds, 30-year O&M contract with VIMHANS Trust) targeted for operations in Q4 FY29-FY30.
Target of about 2,000 operational beds over the next 3-5 years.
Fundraise expected around end-January to early February 2027 after asset finalisation; target is EBITDA-positive acquisitions.
Other income guided at similar levels to Q2 for the rest of FY27, then gradually declining after Q4 FY27.
Oncology drug price-cap risk quantified by management at 0.5% to 0.8% EBITDA impact in a worst case, up to 1-1.25% if extended to all drugs (hypothetical).
risks_watch: Raipur ramp-up: loss-making at about INR 9 crore in first quarter; breakeven guided at 12-15 months depends on occupancy rising from about 10%.
Oncology drug margin cap: policy not yet issued, matter pending in courts; management's quantified worst case is 0.5-0.8% EBITDA.
Fundraise and acquisitions: timing (end-Jan to early Feb 2027) and asset finalisation not yet done; management said targets are EBITDA-positive.
South Delhi project execution in a GRAP-affected NCR environment; operations timeline Q4 FY29-FY30.
Other income of about INR 8 crore per quarter is a meaningful contributor and will decline gradually after Q4 FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on Gurugram margins and Raipur's early ARPOB, with firm timelines on expansion. Evasive on the oncology pricing policy, which management described as hypothetical with no policy yet issued. Specific and quantified on Raipur losses and costs.
key_quotes: We are confident of pushing it up to 75% occupancy and you will, with the cost points remaining more or less the same, so you, you will see a further increase in the EBITDA here as well.
So right now, there is no fear of losing business as of now.
We do not, we do not believe in paying too much for acquiring.

qa_highlights.question: What is Raipur's occupancy and approximate EBITDA loss?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 loss was about INR 9 crore against an estimated INR 9-10 crore, revenue INR 5.3 crore vs INR 4.3 crore estimate, and occupancy about 10% ahead of the official inauguration; ARPOB started at about INR 30,000-32,000 versus competitors at INR 26,000-27,000.

qa_highlights.question: Will Tower 4 at Gurugram add 250 beds in one go or in phases, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all 250 beds will come in one go by H2 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the South Delhi project and its regulatory exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Drawings are submitted to MCD and demolition of the old building is in progress; it is trust land under a 30-year O&M contract with VIMHANS Trust, environment clearance was awaited, and all other compliances are in place. Operations are targeted for Q4 FY29-FY30.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the oncology pricing risk, and how does it compare with the 2017-18 stent pricing episode?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no policy yet and the matter is in court, with no current business loss; worst case is 0.5-0.8% EBITDA impact, and it described this as much smaller than the stent and implant price action.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timing of the fundraise and what is the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said assets are being finalised, the raise is expected around end-January to early February 2027 after post-Diwali target finalisation, and targets are EBITDA-positive.

qa_highlights.question: What are Raipur's operating costs and the outlook for breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating costs were about INR 10 crore including fixed costs in Q2; most costs are already in place with only a few nurses expected to be added. Breakeven remains guided at 12-15 months, with internal aim to beat it.

capex_capacity: Gurugram Tower 4: adds 250 beds within existing campus (supported by additional floor area and Platinum Green Building benefit), all in one phase by H2 FY28; takes beds from about 700 to 900-plus; management cited 220-250 beds range for the tower

South Delhi (Lajpat Nagar): 650-plus bed tertiary/quaternary project under 30-year operation and management contract with VIMHANS Trust on trust land; drawings submitted to MCD, old building demolition in progress; environment clearance was pending; operations targeted Q4 FY29-FY30
Target of about 2,000 operational beds over next 3-5 years, combining Raipur, Gurugram expansion and South Delhi

Raipur Artemis Shanti Hospital: 300 beds (one speaker cited 250 as the figure, then confirmed 300); operations began July 2026 with doctors onboarded from 1 July and theatres/cath lab live from 29 July; grand opening scheduled the following day

Future bed size: new hospitals targeted at 300-350 beds minimum, up to 500; bed cost about INR 50-55 lakh per bed for the first 300 beds at Raipur; focus on Delhi NCR and tier-2 capitals in Central and Eastern India, with combination of greenfield and brownfield acquisitions
Artemis Cardiac Care: 4-5 more units planned after fundraise-funded bigger hospitals, likely from around Q3 next year
demand_pricing: Gurugram: highest-ever Q2 EBITDA margin of 23.8% at 68% occupancy; target 75% occupancy with cost points broadly unchanged

Raipur: occupancy about 10% at time of call; expected to reach 20-25%, possibly 30%, in coming quarters; ARPOB about INR 30,000-32,000 vs competitor benchmark of INR 26,000-27,000; management earlier aspired to INR 55,000-58,000 and said it could exceed this

Raipur Q1 revenue INR 5.3 crore vs INR 4.3 crore internal estimate; loss about INR 9 crore; operating cost about INR 10 crore including fixed costs; started with high-end surgeries rather than general OPD
International patients about 30% of Q2 revenue, from more than 150 countries

Oncology drug price cap: no policy issued yet, matter with courts; management's back-of-envelope worst case 0.5-0.8% EBITDA impact if capped at 20% oncology margin; up to 1-1.25% if extended to all drugs (hypothetical); room tariffs already at 3-star levels so management sees zero impact there
Artemis Cardiac Care: Q2 EBITDA about INR 70 lakh and PAT about INR 20 lakh

growth.why: Management guides Raipur occupancy to 20-25% (possibly 30%) and breakeven in 12-15 months, Gurugram to 75% occupancy, and about 2,000 beds in 3-5 years, backed by commissioned Raipur beds and Tower 4 (250 beds by H2 FY28) and South Delhi (650-plus beds, Q4 FY29-FY30), though the near-term ramp is unproven and the South Delhi approval is still pending.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gurugram hit a record 23.8% EBITDA margin at 68% occupancy and targets 75% with cost points broadly unchanged, but Raipur is loss-making at about INR 9 crore in its first quarter and drags consolidated margin (reported EBITDA 20.2% vs adjusted 23.3%).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q3 FY27 (Raipur live); Tower 4 by H2 FY28
rows.why: Raipur 300 beds already commissioned in July 2026, and Gurugram Tower 4 adds 250 beds in one phase by H2 FY28 (beds from about 700 to 900-plus, +35.7%).

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Raipur occupancy from about 10% guided to 20-25% (possibly 30%) in coming quarters, and Gurugram from 68% to 75%, with H1 FY27 revenue up 13% YoY.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation at Gurugram is 68%, and the fundraise (end-Jan to early Feb 2027) is targeted at bigger 300-350+ bed hospitals at about INR 50-55 lakh per bed, with 4-5 more cardiac units planned from around Q3 next year.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management says Raipur breakeven at 12-15 months has an internal aim to beat it, and ARPOB at INR 30,000-32,000 is above the INR 26,000-27,000 competitor benchmark, with ramp toward INR 55,000-58,000 noted as possible.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Raipur occupancy is only about 10% against a 20-25% ramp target and a loss of about INR 9 crore per quarter, and other income of about INR 8 crore per quarter declines after Q4 FY27.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Artemis Cardiac Care plans 4-5 more units after the fundraise-funded bigger hospitals, likely from around Q3 next year; the call gives no new drug or molecule launch.

rows.label: Oncology drug price cap
rows.why: No policy issued yet and the matter is in court; management's worst case is 0.5-0.8% EBITDA impact if capped at 20% oncology margin, and up to 1-1.25% if extended to all drugs (hypothetical).

rows.label: Fundraise for EBITDA-positive acquisitions
rows.why: Assets are being finalised and the raise is targeted around end-January to early February 2027, with the aim of EBITDA-positive acquisitions to add capacity toward about 2,000 beds in 3-5 years.

rows.label: South Delhi Lajpat Nagar 650-plus bed hospital
rows.why: Drawings submitted to MCD and old building demolition under way on a 30-year O&M contract with VIMHANS Trust, but environment clearance was pending and operations are targeted for Q4 FY29-FY30, outside the window.

tone.note: Management was confident on Gurugram margins (record 23.8%), Raipur early ARPOB and firm expansion timelines, and cautious on the oncology pricing policy, which it called hypothetical; analysts pressed on Raipur losses, occupancy ramp and the oncology price-cap exposure.
